title: [finding] `packages/qa/dogfood/tsconfig.json`: the rootDir comment opens "No `rootDir`." directly above a line that sets one
body:
## What

At `origin/main` `b3723188`, `packages/qa/dogfood/tsconfig.json` reads:

```jsonc
    "types": ["node"],
    // No `rootDir`. This project emits nothing (`noEmit`), so `rootDir` never
    // shaped an output layout here — its only effect was to forbid importing a
    // sibling package's SOURCE file, and the route-ledger ↔ live-mount parity
    // gate (#7526) must read the five ledgers exactly that way: each one is
    // package-internal on purpose (the guard's data, not public API), so there
    // is no entry point to import them from. Every other ledger guard in the
    // repo compiles them as relative sources for the same reason.
    "rootDir": "../../.."
```

The comment opens `// No `rootDir`.` and the line it sits on top of sets one.

## Impact, stated honestly: cosmetic, and nothing is broken

The comment's **argument** still holds under the declaration that is actually
there: it wants sibling packages' source files to be legal program inputs, and
an explicit repo-root `rootDir` gives exactly that — every input file in this
program is under `../../..`, so the constraint the comment describes as harmful
never fires. There is no build or typecheck consequence, and no gate reads it.

What is wrong is only the first sentence, which tells the next reader there is
no `rootDir` two lines above one. This is a load-bearing spot precisely because
the rest of the comment is careful and correct: it is cited to future authors as
a deliberate, reasoned shape, so a reader who greps for the decision finds a
declaration and a denial of that declaration in the same seven lines and cannot
tell which one is current.

## Provenance deliberately not claimed

This checkout is shallow (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = `true`, 92
commits), and `git blame` on those lines lands on the boundary commit. Whether
`rootDir` was re-added after the comment was written, or the comment was written
for a form the file no longer has, is not answerable from here — someone with
full history should establish it before rewriting the text, since the two
readings imply different fixes (drop the first sentence vs drop the `rootDir`).

## Possible dispositions, for triage rather than as a recommendation

1. Drop or rewrite the opening sentence so the prose matches the declaration.
2. Remove `rootDir` and keep the comment as written — only if full history shows
   that was the intended state; behaviour here would be equivalent, but this is
   the larger claim and needs the history the finder did not have.
3. Leave it — the argument is correct and the mismatch is one sentence.

Found while implementing #10899, whose ruling scopes that PR to the dead
`include` glob and explicitly forbids tidying anything else in this file, so it
was deliberately left untouched there. Unassigned, and not queued.
